Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as three files on 2026-10-30: a photo of the paper scorecard grid, the app scorecard PDF, and the full graded play-by-play text; official R1-08 Game 3 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Box score record: the three sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every number subject to one scoring settlement, documented below. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log (Babe Adams pitched a complete game, the only Pittsburgh pitcher, and takes the win; Jimmy Key was charged with all 7 Pittsburgh runs and took the loss; Roberto Osuna, Duane Ward, and Tom Henke each threw one scoreless inning of relief; there is no save in a complete game win). Pittsburgh struck first: Roberto Clemente and Barry Bonds hit back-to-back home runs in the Top 1 for 2-0. Toronto answered in the Bottom 1: Tony Fernandez doubled, Carlos Delgado walked, and Fred McGriff doubled both in for 2-2. Clemente doubled in the Top 4, Willie Stargell walked, and Ralph Kiner's sacrifice fly made it 3-2. Toronto tied it again in the Bottom 4: McGriff doubled a second time and Jesse Barfield singled him in, 3-3. Tommy Leach tripled to open the Top 5 and Honus Wagner's groundout scored him for 4-3. The Top 6 settled the game: Clemente walked, Bonds singled him to 3rd, Stargell flew out, Clemente scored (on Key's wild pitch; see the settlement below), Kiner flew out to right, and Manny Sanguillen hit a 2-run home run for 7-3. Adams allowed nothing after the 4th; over the last five innings his only baserunners were Delgado's double in the 6th, Delgado's walk in the 8th, and Barfield's double in the 9th. The scoring settlement: Pittsburgh's printed RBI total is 6 against 7 runs. Kiner's line is 3 at-bats, 1 RBI, and one sacrifice fly, the Top 4 fly that scored Clemente, narrated as a sacrifice fly in the play log. In the Top 6 the play log attaches the score change (PIT 5) to Kiner's flyout line, but the scorecard counts that at-bat as a plain flyout (an at-bat, no sacrifice fly, no RBI) and charges Key with a wild pitch (WP 1, printed on the card).
